migrations.title: Migration 0002 — support lookups
migrations.description: Gives every rental a short customer-facing reference and makes receipt-email matching case-insensitive and indexed. Lookups run server-side (service role) and require an exact email match, so they can't be used to enumerate other customers' rentals.

migrations.title: Migration 0003 — refund totals on payments
migrations.description: Kept in sync by the (future) Stripe webhook so support can show captured vs refunded amounts. Stripe's live API remains the source of truth when linked (see src/lib/payments/source.ts).

migrations.title: Migration 0004 — helpdesk operations
migrations.description: Threaded tickets with AI/human handling state, SLA clocks, queues, partner (venue) requests, refund workflow (request → approve → issue) with a one-open-per-rental guard, audit timeline, and an email outbox. All writes go through server-side code using the service role.

migrations.title: Migration 0005 — security lockdown
migrations.description: Live-audit findings: `for all` policies let any signed-in user update their own profile (role escalation to admin) and let partners rewrite their own agreements, ledgers, venues and hardware rows. Non-staff now get SELECT-only; all writes go through the service layer (service role), never a user's own JWT.

migrations.title: Migration 0006 — only the service layer writes
migrations.description: Staff JWTs previously had `for all` policies: a stolen or misused staff token could insert an 'approved' refund_request, flip internal notes public, or edit tickets directly via PostgREST — bypassing service-layer validation, the second-person refund rule, and the audit trail. The app only ever writes via the service role (which bypasses RLS), so every JWT policy becomes SELECT-only.

migrations.title: Migration 0007 — branded HTML email bodies in the outbox.
migrations.description: body keeps the plain-text fallback; html carries the rendered design-system template.
